ch07.card: Part 6 of 8. Writing down the answer.
ch07.s01.c1: This is the last stop on the map: the talker.
ch07.s01.c2: Its only job is to write the final answer. It adds no thinking.
ch07.s01.c3: It reads the thinker's final state, and may copy from the question and the calculator's replies.
ch07.s01.c4: But only where the thinker points. Today's talker is a small stand-in.
ch07.s02.c1: Today's talker is a small stand-in with three ways to write an answer.
ch07.s02.c2: Span copy takes a stretch of letters from the question or a reply.
ch07.s02.c3: A word pointer, a learned pick of a spot, takes one whole word from the question.
ch07.s02.c4: Letter slots spell the answer when it is not in the text.
ch07.s03.c1: The thinker's final state sets a pointer on the last digit of the last reply: the 0.
ch07.s03.c2: The copy steps one letter left and takes the 1.
ch07.s03.c3: Next to the left is a space. A small learned part, the stop head, says stop.
ch07.s03.c4: The digits came out last first, 0 then 1. Plain code flips them to read 10.
ch07.s04.c1: In all 6 copies of the 3-million-number model with an outside calculator (T1SDR), span copy wrote 91.5% of answers.
ch07.s04.c2: That counts how often it was used on 400 familiar calculator questions, not how often it was right.
ch07.s04.c3: The pointer and the stop head are learned. Three small pieces are still hand-written code.
ch07.s04.c4: The plan: one learned writer replaces them. That build has not been run.
ch07.s05.c1: When the answer is not in the text, the talker spells it in letter slots.
ch07.s05.c2: Today there are 9 places: room for 8 letters and an end mark. Each place picks a letter, or copies one.
ch07.s05.c3: They fill last letter first, so yes comes out as s, e, y. The code flips it.
ch07.s06.c1: Today's letter slots hold 8 letters. A longer training answer would be cut to 8.
ch07.s06.c2: That never happened: 0 of 200,000 training answers were longer than 8.
ch07.s06.c3: But hiding a word of 9 to 12 letters, in fill-in-the-blank practice, would hit it.
ch07.s06.c4: The finished design (B3) writes up to 35 letters and counts any longer answer.
ch07.s06.c5: A count above 0 fails its pass mark, set in advance. Blanks of 9 to 12 letters are safe only here.
ch07.s07.c1: The finished plan has a real talker of about 25 million numbers (25M) that writes English.
ch07.s07.c2: It is not built. As built, the 100M-thinker design is 373.1M in all: 271.0M borrowed, frozen reader (Gemma) plus 102.1M trained.
ch07.s07.c3: How it would learn to write English is not in the plan. A separate team session owns that.
ch07.s08.c1: These tests are older, from a design built on borrowed language models. Not today's talker.
ch07.s08.c2: With a 350-million-number language model as reader and talker, our system scored 66.1. With 1.2 billion: 92.6.
ch07.s08.c3: A small copy talker scored 13.6 on question kinds it never practised. The language-model talker scored 78.2.
ch07.s09.c1: One check turned the thinking off on one trained copy at 3M. This is the older design: calculator inside, 12 rounds.
ch07.s09.c2: Thinking on scored 73.01. Thinking off scored 0.66, on 6,040 questions kept aside.
ch07.s09.c3: That hints the talker cannot answer alone. One copy is only a hint.
ch07.s09.c4: An earlier Gemma-reader copy scored 18.09 on familiar questions with zero rounds, so 'cannot' is not shown.
ch07.s10.c1: Free web text, called FineWeb-Edu, enters practice as fill-in-the-blank rows.
ch07.s10.c2: One word of 3 to 12 letters is hidden, and the model must name it.
ch07.s10.c3: So this kind of practice teaches reading English, not writing it.
ch07.s10.c4: By plan, 84% of the practice text in the planned big training run is web text.
ch07.s11.c1: The plan's final proof is a race against small public models, such as SmolLM2-360M.
ch07.s11.c2: To win, it must be ahead by at least 3 points on our own kept-aside tests, and ahead on a question set called bAbI.
ch07.s11.c3: The whole size is counted, borrowed numbers too. The race needs the English talker, which does not exist yet.
ch07.s12.c1: It writes only the final answer, copying where the thinker points.
ch07.s12.c2: Today it is a small stand-in, tested only inside the 3M runs.
ch07.s12.c3: The English talker is a placeholder. Today's model gives short answers, not sentences.
